layer_reason: Failure is not arithmetic or tiling: the SPLIT_QK applicability predicate at host metadata level (candidate.py:430-431) gates a compile-time branch whose K loads are deliberately unmasked. It tests the padded BLOCK_D==128 but not the true channel count D==128. BLOCK_D=next_power_of_2(D) is 128 for any D in 65..127, so such metadata passes the predicate, enters the split branch, and issues two unmasked 128-wide K loads that read channels D..127 beyond the real head width; MASK_KV is simultaneously true (D != BLOCK_D) and the V path references kv_mask, which is only defined inside the non-split MASK_KV branch, so the compile path is also ill-defined. The fix belongs in the same metadata predicate, not in the kernel body or tiling.

evidence.finding: Source review status=source_review_repair_required; issue states SPLIT_QK predicate uses padded BLOCK_D==128 rather than requiring actualD==128; unmasked splitK loads can exceed actual channel bounds and MASK_KV path uses undefined kv_mask. device_evaluation_started=false. requested_repair: require actualD==128 in the same metadata predicate, preserve all other computations/paths.

Host analysis confirms the address-range gap: BLOCK_D==128 alone admits actualD 65..127, split-QK K loads are unmasked and assume exactly 128 valid channels, and MASK_KV also becomes true while kv_mask is defined only in the normal QK branch. Host requests D==128 be added to the same SPLIT_QK predicate and the EXACT_UNGUARDED description updated; current arithmetic, concat column order, main kernel AST and other branches preserved; no new operator tests.

SPLIT_QK = (value.dtype==bf16) and (not is_causal) and (BLOCK_D==128) and (SKV==256) and (S%256==0). BLOCK_D is computed at line 422 as max(16,next_power_of_2(D)); the predicate never checks D itself.

Split branch loads k_lo/k_hi with tl.load(k_ptrs_lo)/tl.load(k_ptrs_hi) (no mask) and then falls through to the shared V load guarded by 'if MASK_KV': kv_mask. With D<BLOCK_D, MASK_KV is true but kv_mask was only defined in the non-split 'if MASK_KV' block at lines 260-262, so the split branch both over-reads channels and references an undefined mask.

EXACT_UNGUARDED = SPLIT_QK and MASK_MD/MASK_KV are derived from D==BLOCK_D. Once SPLIT_QK requires D==128, then D==BLOCK_D holds and with SKV==BLOCK_N==256 and S%256==0 both MASK_KV and MASK_MD are statically False, so every unmasked load/store and every removed guard is justified.

Parent-geometry TTIR (D=128, SKV=256, S%256==0, BLOCK_M=128 non-split path) shows the 128x256 QK dot and unmasked 256x128 bf16 K load / 256x128 f16 V load with 128-wide channel tensors, confirming the D==128/SKV==256 geometry on which the split specialisation is defined. This IR predates the current source edit and is not a build of the split candidate.

BCMLIR for the same parent geometry shows memref sizes [256,128] / [128,128] with inner stride 1, i.e. exactly 128 valid channels and no channel mask, matching the assumption the SPLIT_QK branch makes (and that becomes provable only when D==128).
All four fixed cases 1,2,4,7 have D=128, so none is in the latent 65..127 hole; the repair must not alter the evaluated numerics or timing for these cases.
